Here is a complete, highly structured 50-minute lesson plan designed for the realities of a busy state school classroom. It is designed to be high-impact, low-prep, and fully differentiated. --- # Lesson Plan: The Powder Keg of Europe – Causes of WWI * **Subject:** History (KS3 / Year 9) * **Class Size:** 34 students (Wide attainment spread; 6 students with reading ages below 9) * **Resources:** Projector (for slides), 34 copies of the double-sided A4 worksheet (provided below). No student devices. --- ## Learning Objectives 1. **Identify** the four long-term causes of WWI (M-A-I-N). 2. **Explain** how the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand acted as the "spark" to the "powder keg". 3. **Evaluate** which cause was the most significant in starting the war. --- ## Lesson Timings (50 Minutes) ### 00:00 – 00:05 | Hook & Retrieval (5 mins) * **Teacher Action:** Project an image of a giant wooden barrel of gunpowder with a lit fuse (the "Powder Keg" analogy). Ask: *"If this barrel explodes, is it the fault of the gunpowder inside, or the spark that lit it?"* * **Student Action:** Think-Pair-Share. * **Differentiation:** The visual analogy allows lower-attaining students to access the concept of "underlying causes" vs. "immediate triggers" without reading barriers. ### 00:05 – 00:15 | Direct Instruction: The M-A-I-N Causes (10 mins) * **Teacher Action:** Hand out the A4 worksheet. Project four slides, each representing one letter of **M-A-I-N** (Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism). Keep explanations brief, using the icons on the worksheet to dual-code the information. * *Militarism:* The arms race (building bigger navies). * *Alliances:* Friendships/promises to fight together. * *Imperialism:* Fighting over colonies in Africa. * *Nationalism:* Extreme pride in your country. * **Check for Understanding (Cold Call):** *"Jordan, if Germany builds 10 new battleships and Britain builds 12, which letter of M-A-I-N is that?"* ### 00:15 – 00:30 | Guided Reading & Categorisation (15 mins) * **Student Action:** Students read **Side A** of the worksheet. * **Differentiation in Action:** * **Reading Age < 9 Support:** Pair these 6 students with supportive peers, or seat them as a small group with the teacher/TA to read the simplified text aloud. The text uses short sentences, bold key terms, and a built-in glossary. * **Task:** Students complete **Task 1 (The M-A-I-N Grid)** on Side B, categorising the historical facts. * **Teacher Action:** Circulate the room, checking that the 6 target students have correctly identified at least one fact for each letter. ### 00:30 – 00:42 | The Spark & The Chain Reaction (12 mins) * **Teacher Action:** Project a simple map of Europe in 1914. Explain the "Spark": The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo. Explain how the Alliance system dragged everyone in like a domino effect. * **Student Action:** Students complete **Task 2 (The Chain Reaction)** on Side B. They must fill in the blanks to show how the spark exploded the powder keg. * **Stretch & Challenge (Higher Attainers):** Complete **Task 3 (The Big Question)**: *"Which of the M-A-I-N causes was the most dangerous, and why?"* ### 00:42 – 00:48 | Plenary & Checking for Understanding (6 mins) * **Student Action:** Students complete the **Exit Ticket** at the bottom of Side B. They must tear/cut off this slip and hand it to the teacher as they leave the room. * **Teacher Action:** Stand at the door to collect the slips. This gives you 34 pieces of instant data to assess learning before the next lesson. ### 00:48 – 00:50 | Pack Up & Dismissal (2 mins) * Stand at the door, collect exit tickets, and dismiss students orderly. --- # The Printed Resource (Double-Sided A4) *Instructions for printing: Print this double-sided on one sheet of A4 paper per student.* --- ## [SIDE A - READ ME] ### The Causes of World War I (1914) In 1914, Europe was like a **powder keg** (a barrel of gunpowder). It was highly explosive and waiting to blow up. There were four long-term causes of this tension. We remember them using the word **M-A-I-N**. #### ⚔️ M – Militarism (Building up armies) Countries in Europe were in an "arms race." They competed to see who could build the biggest army and navy. Germany and Britain both wanted the strongest navy in the world. This made countries suspicious and scared of each other. #### 🤝 A – Alliances (Making promises) European countries made secret agreements to protect each other. They split into two main groups: * **The Triple Entente:** Britain, France, and Russia. * **The Triple Alliance:** Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy. If one country went to war, their allies promised to jump in and help them. #### 👑 I – Imperialism (Building empires) European countries wanted to rule other parts of the world. They competed to take over land in Africa and Asia. This competition caused fierce arguments and jealousy, especially between Britain and Germany. #### 🦁 N – Nationalism (Extreme pride) People in Europe were extremely proud of their own countries. They believed their nation was better than all others. Some small groups of people also wanted their own independence, such as the Serbians living inside the Austro-Hungarian Empire. --- ### ⚡ The Spark: The Assassination On **28th June 1914**, Archduke Franz Ferdinand (the heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary) visited the city of Sarajevo. A young Serbian nationalist named Gavrilo Princip shot and killed him and his wife. Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia for the murder and declared war. Because of the **Alliances**, Russia stepped in to help Serbia. Germany then joined to help Austria-Hungary. Within weeks, the whole of Europe was at war. --- ### 📖 Glossary (Key Words) * **Allies:** Friends who promise to help you in a fight. * **Empire:** A group of countries ruled by one powerful nation. * **Tension:** A feeling of fear and anger between groups before a fight. * **Assassination:** The murder of an important leader. --- ## [SIDE B - WORK ON ME] **Name:** ___________________________ **Class:** Year 9 ### Task 1: The M-A-I-N Grid *Read Side A. Write **one** short sentence of evidence for each letter in the boxes below.* | **M**ilitarism (Armies/Navies) | **A**lliances (Friendships) | | :--- | :--- | | *e.g., Germany and Britain competed to build...*


| *e.g., The two main groups were...*


| | **I**mperialism (Empires) | **N**ationalism (Pride) | | *e.g., European countries fought over land in...*


| *e.g., People believed their country was...*


| --- ### Task 2: The Chain Reaction (Fill in the blanks) *Use the words in the box to complete the story of how the war started.* > **Words:** Allies | Spark | Sarajevo | Shot | Germany In June 1914, Archduke Franz Ferdinand was _______________ in the city of _______________. This event was the _______________ that lit the powder keg. Austria-Hungary declared war. Because of the _______________ system, other countries were dragged in. _______________ joined to help Austria-Hungary, and soon all of Europe was at war. --- ### Task 3: The Big Question (Stretch & Challenge) *Which of the M-A-I-N causes do you think was the most dangerous? Explain your answer.* I think ________________________ was the most dangerous cause because __________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ --- ✂️ *------------------ TEAR OFF HERE AND HAND TO THE TEACHER AT THE DOOR ------------------* ### EXIT TICKET **1. What does the 'A' in M-A-I-N stand for?** * [ ] Armies * [ ] Alliances * [ ] Arguments **2. Who was assassinated to spark World War I?** * [ ] The King of Germany * [ ] Archduke Franz Ferdinand * [ ] Gavrilo Princip **3. In your own words, why did a fight between just two countries (Austria and Serbia) turn into a massive World War?** __________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
